samples.summary: The URL printed for copy-paste omits `cliState`, so copying it makes the login fail with a misleading "upgrade the server" message
samples.evidence: login.ts:71-76 builds `oauthUrl` with `&cliState=<nonce>` but prints `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}` — the nonce-less form. If the user visits that printed URL (docs/design/cli.md:176 still documents step 3 as "also prints URL for copy-paste in headless environments"), the backend guard receives `cliState === undefined`, `normalizeCliState` returns undefined, `createState(mode, port, undefined)` stores a nonce-less flow, and auth.controller.ts:130-134 redirects to `127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=…` with NO `state`. The CLI's listener then takes the `received === null && !options.allowUnbound` branch (login.ts:263) and REJECTS the login with UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE, which tells the user to "Upgrade the server, or re-run with --allow-unbound-callback" — a false diagnosis, since the server is fine and the real cause is that the CLI printed a URL it will not accept the callback for. The login is settled, so it cannot recover.

samples.summary: The usable OAuth URL is now printed only when `open()` throws, so a headless/no-browser environment can be left with no way to continue
samples.evidence: The old code printed the full URL unconditionally plus "If the browser does not open, visit the URL above."; the new code prints the full URL only inside `catch` around `await open(oauthUrl)` (login.ts:78-87). `open()` with the default `wait: false` resolves as soon as the child is spawned and does not reject when the spawned handler (e.g. `xdg-open` under SSH/WSL/headless) fails to surface a browser — and a later child `error` event is not routed to this promise at all. In those cases nothing prints the nonce-carrying URL, and the login dies on the 30-second timeout with "Login timed out", while the only URL the user was shown (line 75) is the nonce-less one that cannot complete the flow (see the previous finding).

samples.summary: New `callbackReject` on a nonce-less callback can fire before any handler is attached, turning an actionable failure into an unhandled-rejection crash
samples.evidence: `callbackPromise` (login.ts:235) gets no handler until the action reaches `await waitForCallback()` at line 92, which is after `await import('open')` and `await open(oauthUrl)`. The new branch at login.ts:263-271 rejects that promise from the HTTP handler. Any `GET /callback?code=…` without `state` arriving during that window — trivially producible by any other local process racing the loopback port, and possible for a fast browser leg — rejects an unhandled promise, so Node terminates the process with ERR_UNHANDLED_REJECTION instead of emitting UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE through `runCli`'s error envelope. The pre-existing timeout rejection could not hit this window (30 s), so the race is introduced by this change.

samples.summary: `DOT_SEGMENT`'s `%2e` alternatives are dead: the regex is tested against the already-encoded value, so the documented `%2e`/`.%2e` refusals never happen
samples.evidence: `seg()` tests `DOT_SEGMENT.test(encoded)` where `encoded = encodeURIComponent(value)` (url.ts:45-46). `encodeURIComponent` always escapes `%` to `%25`, so no input can ever produce `%2e` in `encoded`; only literal `.` and `..` match. The doc comment at url.ts:4-11 claims an identifier that is `%2e`, `.%2e`, `%2e.` or `%2e%2e` "has to be refused, not escaped", but `seg('%2e%2e')` returns `%252e%252e` (the test at packages/cli/test/http-client-paths.test.ts even asserts this neutralisation). Behaviour is safe, but the guard's stated contract and its implementation disagree, which will mislead the next person who edits the order of encode/test.

samples.summary: Some new `--dry-run` branches sit outside the command's try/catch, so `seg()` failures escape the action instead of being enveloped locally
samples.evidence: `docs get` (docs.ts:126-129), `docs rename` (145), `docs delete` (163), `tabs list` (tabs.ts:15-18) and `cells get` (cells.ts:21-33) call `printDryRun(... seg(docId) ...)` before their `try`, while the sibling commands (`api-keys revoke`, `notes get`, `files get`, `sheets export`) do it inside. For a rejected identifier the first group throws out of the action handler — the new test acknowledges this by using `rejects.toThrow` for `docs get ..` while asserting the printed envelope and `process.exitCode === 1` for `api-keys revoke ..` (packages/cli/test/read-dry-run.test.ts). `runCli` does catch it in the shipped binary, so the user-visible envelope is the same, but any caller that drives `program.parseAsync` directly (as these tests do) gets a rejection from one command and an envelope from another for the same class of input.

samples.summary: The reworked fail-safe test no longer exercises the behaviour it documents: with push-to-main set, the empty-string branch cannot fail the assertion
samples.evidence: The case's own comment (lines ~708-715) states the point is that an empty `WAFFLEBASE_CHANGED_AREAS` must be *ignored* so resolution continues. By adding `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME: "push"` / `GITHUB_REF_NAME: "main"`, `resolve()` returns FULL from the push-to-main gate (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:530) regardless of how the empty string is handled — even a regression that parsed `""` and returned `{ full: undefined }` would be short-circuited or fall through to FULL, so `assert.equal(out.full, true)` and the new `/push to main/` match both pass. The fail-safe the case was written for is now unguarded.
searchedFor: scripts/changed-areas.mjs resolve() ordering of WAFFLEBASE_CHANGED_AREAS vs push-to-main gate

finding.summary: The URL printed for copy-paste omits `cliState`, so copying it makes the login fail with a misleading "upgrade the server" message
finding.evidence: login.ts:71-76 builds `oauthUrl` with `&cliState=<nonce>` but prints `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}` — the nonce-less form. If the user visits that printed URL (docs/design/cli.md:176 still documents step 3 as "also prints URL for copy-paste in headless environments"), the backend guard receives `cliState === undefined`, `normalizeCliState` returns undefined, `createState(mode, port, undefined)` stores a nonce-less flow, and auth.controller.ts:130-134 redirects to `127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=…` with NO `state`. The CLI's listener then takes the `received === null && !options.allowUnbound` branch (login.ts:263) and REJECTS the login with UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE, which tells the user to "Upgrade the server, or re-run with --allow-unbound-callback" — a false diagnosis, since the server is fine and the real cause is that the CLI printed a URL it will not accept the callback for. verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the repo. login.ts:71-76 builds `oauthUrl` with `&cliState=<nonce>` but the `Opening browser:` line prints the nonce-less form; the full URL is printed only in the `catch` at login.ts:82-87, which fires only if `open()` throws — `open()` defaults to `wait: false` and resolves once the child spawns, so on a headless/remote host (xdg-open present, no display) the redacted URL is the only one the user sees. If that URL is used, github-auth.guard.ts:25-26 has `normalizeCliState` return `undefined` for an absent param (explicitly legitimate, not an error) and :70-76 stores a nonce-less flow via `createState(mode, portNum, undefined)`. auth.controller.ts:130-134 then computes `nonce = state.cliState ? ... : ''` and redirects to `127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=…` with no `state`. login.ts:263-271 takes the `received === null && !options.allowUnbound` branch, sets `settled = true` and rejects with UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE (login.ts:216-220), which blames the server ("Upgrade the server, or re-run with --allow-unbound-callback") though the server behaved correctly for the URL it received; the login is settled so it cannot recover. docs/design/cli.md:175-176 still documents step 3 as "also prints URL for copy-paste in headless environments", contradicting the redaction rationale at cli.md:211-214 and inviting exactly this misuse. No guard elsewhere blocks the path and the issue (mis-handled failure / misleading error on a broken login flow) is within the correctness lane, so no named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: The usable OAuth URL is now printed only when `open()` throws, so a headless/no-browser environment can be left with no way to continue
finding.evidence: The old code printed the full URL unconditionally plus "If the browser does not open, visit the URL above."; the new code prints the full URL only inside `catch` around `await open(oauthUrl)` (login.ts:78-87). `open()` with the default `wait: false` resolves as soon as the child is spawned and does not reject when the spawned handler (e.g. `xdg-open` under SSH/WSL/headless) fails to surface a browser — and a later child `error` event is not routed to this promise at all. In those cases nothing prints the nonce-carrying URL, and the login dies on the 30-second timeout with "Login timed out", while the only URL the user was shown (line 75) is the nonce-less one that cannot complete the flow (see the previous finding).

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository: login.ts:71-76 prints only a nonce-less URL unconditionally, while the usable nonce-carrying `oauthUrl` is printed solely inside the `catch` at login.ts:81-87. The dependency is `open` ^11.0.0 (packages/cli/package.json:28), whose default non-waiting mode resolves as soon as the handler is spawned and does not reject when the spawned handler fails to surface a browser, so the catch-only fallback does not fire in headless/SSH/WSL cases. The user is then left with a URL lacking `cliState`, which the callback server explicitly rejects at login.ts:263-271 (UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE) absent `--allow-unbound-callback`, and the login dies on the 30s timeout at login.ts:327-335. No TTY/DISPLAY/BROWSER detection, no `--print-url`/`--no-browser` option (only `--allow-unbound-callback` is registered at login.ts:17-21), and no other site prints the full URL. This is a real, reachable break of a core flow with mis-handled failure detection, within the correctness lane; no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: New `callbackReject` on a nonce-less callback can fire before any handler is attached, turning an actionable failure into an unhandled-rejection crash
finding.evidence: `callbackPromise` (login.ts:235) gets no handler until the action reaches `await waitForCallback()` at line 92, which is after `await import('open')` and `await open(oauthUrl)`. The new branch at login.ts:263-271 rejects that promise from the HTTP handler. Any `GET /callback?code=…` without `state` arriving during that window — trivially producible by any other local process racing the loopback port, and possible for a fast browser leg — rejects an unhandled promise, so Node terminates the process with ERR_UNHANDLED_REJECTION instead of emitting UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE through `runCli`'s error envelope. The pre-existing timeout rejection could not hit this window (30 s), so the race is introduced by this change.

verdict.reason: The described code exists verbatim. callbackPromise is created with no subscriber (login.ts:235-238) and is only consumed lazily via `waitForCallback: () => callbackPromise` (login.ts:349), whose first call is at login.ts:92 — after `await import('open')` (line 79) and `await open(oauthUrl)` (line 80), both of which cross macrotask boundaries. The new no-`state` branch (login.ts:263-271) rejects that promise from inside the HTTP request handler, and the server has been listening since login.ts:59, so a `GET /callback?code=…` without `state` arriving in that window rejects a promise with no handler attached. No mitigation exists: there is no process-level unhandledRejection/uncaughtException handler anywhere in packages/cli (src/bin.ts:6 is just `void runCli()`), and runCli's try/catch (cli.ts:75-91) only envelopes rejections propagated through parseAsync — it cannot catch an unawaited promise. Result is ERR_UNHANDLED_REJECTION process termination instead of the UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE error envelope, and the `finally { close() }` at login.ts:93-95 never runs. The other settle sites are not exposed the same way (timeout fires at 30 s, login.ts:327-335; the wrong-state branch at login.ts:276-280 deliberately does not settle), so the window is specific to this branch. Real, in-lane (missing guard causing a crash on a reachable path); no named ground to refute.
